references.source:
Kishore Kumar Vunnamatla, Mathews John, and Nelson Samuvel\.
The nimadi\-speaking people of madhya pradesh: a sociolinguistic profile\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012\-002, SIL International, Dallas, Texas, 2012\.
The report states that the vowel symbols schwa, turned v, script a and alpha are interchangeable for its purposes and assumes no phonemic distinction among them\. Source IPA remains in Original/Phonemic while a dedicated display profile applies Jambu conventions\. Lexical\-similarity category numbers are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. Three unusual forms containing literal capital B are preserved in source transcription and normalize to lowercase b in display\. The PDF text\-layer artifact cid:1 at Gujarati item 98 and the category/blank\-cell artifacts at Nimadi items 13 and 40 were checked against rendered source pages and documented per record\. Appendix A supplies locality, administrative and community metadata but no coordinates, so all thirteen dialect records intentionally leave coordinates blank\.
URL: [http://www\-01\.sil\.org/silesr/2012/silesr2012\-002\.pdf](http://www-01.sil.org/silesr/2012/silesr2012-002.pdf)\.
references.progress: Appendix A, printed pages 57--100: every nonempty lexical response from the thirteen newly elicited Nimadi lists. Excludes five target cells explicitly printed as no entry, one target cell without a printed response row, one target cell with a blank primary response but retains its printed alternate, the Parya Bhilali and Malvi borrowed comparison lists, the Hindi, Gujarati and Marathi standard controls, and prompts 11 breast, 23 urine, 24 feces and 70 millet which are absent from the published appendix
references.provenance: The exact official publisher PDF was recovered through Internet Archive capture 20170810011221 because the legacy SIL URL no longer serves the file directly; PDF SHA-256 1a7e8daaeb2b967e2f9490292689e33a188caf47dc262c942a47136bb270d0d8. The PDF is not redistributed. Reproducible text-layer extraction and checked snapshot are in data/other/forms/raw_data/sil_nimadi_2012; complete per-record audit is data/other/forms/raw_data/20260828-sil-nimadi-audit.csv; installed rows are data/other/forms/20260828-sil-nimadi.csv

references.source:
Kishore Kumar Vunnamatla, Mathews John, and Nelson Samuvel\.
The nimadi\-speaking people of madhya pradesh: a sociolinguistic profile\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012\-002, SIL International, Dallas, Texas, 2012\.
The report states that the vowel symbols schwa, turned v, script a and alpha are interchangeable for its purposes and assumes no phonemic distinction among them\. Source IPA remains in Original/Phonemic while a dedicated display profile applies Jambu conventions\. Lexical\-similarity category numbers are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. Three unusual forms containing literal capital B are preserved in source transcription and normalize to lowercase b in display\. The PDF text\-layer artifact cid:1 at Gujarati item 98 and the category/blank\-cell artifacts at Nimadi items 13 and 40 were checked against rendered source pages and documented per record\. Appendix A supplies locality, administrative and community metadata but no coordinates, so all thirteen dialect records intentionally leave coordinates blank\.
URL: [http://www\-01\.sil\.org/silesr/2012/silesr2012\-002\.pdf](http://www-01.sil.org/silesr/2012/silesr2012-002.pdf)\.
references.progress: Appendix A, printed pages 57--100: every nonempty lexical response from the thirteen newly elicited Nimadi lists. Excludes five target cells explicitly printed as no entry, one target cell without a printed response row, one target cell with a blank primary response but retains its printed alternate, the Parya Bhilali and Malvi borrowed comparison lists, the Hindi, Gujarati and Marathi standard controls, and prompts 11 breast, 23 urine, 24 feces and 70 millet which are absent from the published appendix

The nimadi\-speaking people of madhya pradesh: a sociolinguistic profile\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012\-002, SIL International, Dallas, Texas, 2012\.
The report states that the vowel symbols schwa, turned v, script a and alpha are interchangeable for its purposes and assumes no phonemic distinction among them\. Source IPA remains in Original/Phonemic while a dedicated display profile applies Jambu conventions\. Lexical\-similarity category numbers are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. Three unusual forms containing literal capital B are preserved in source transcription and normalize to lowercase b in display\. The PDF text\-layer artifact cid:1 at Gujarati item 98 and the category/blank\-cell artifacts at Nimadi items 13 and 40 were checked against rendered source pages and documented per record\. Appendix A supplies locality, administrative and community metadata but no coordinates, so all thirteen dialect records intentionally leave coordinates blank\.
URL: [http://www\-01\.sil\.org/silesr/2012/silesr2012\-002\.pdf](http://www-01.sil.org/silesr/2012/silesr2012-002.pdf)\.
references.progress: Appendix A, printed pages 57--100: every nonempty lexical response from the thirteen newly elicited Nimadi lists. Excludes five target cells explicitly printed as no entry, one target cell without a printed response row, one target cell with a blank primary response but retains its printed alternate, the Parya Bhilali and Malvi borrowed comparison lists, the Hindi, Gujarati and Marathi standard controls, and prompts 11 breast, 23 urine, 24 feces and 70 millet which are absent from the published appendix

The nimadi\-speaking people of madhya pradesh: a sociolinguistic profile\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012\-002, SIL International, Dallas, Texas, 2012\.
The report states that the vowel symbols schwa, turned v, script a and alpha are interchangeable for its purposes and assumes no phonemic distinction among them\. Source IPA remains in Original/Phonemic while a dedicated display profile applies Jambu conventions\. Lexical\-similarity category numbers are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. Three unusual forms containing literal capital B are preserved in source transcription and normalize to lowercase b in display\. The PDF text\-layer artifact cid:1 at Gujarati item 98 and the category/blank\-cell artifacts at Nimadi items 13 and 40 were checked against rendered source pages and documented per record\. Appendix A supplies locality, administrative and community metadata but no coordinates, so all thirteen dialect records intentionally leave coordinates blank\.
URL: [http://www\-01\.sil\.org/silesr/2012/silesr2012\-002\.pdf](http://www-01.sil.org/silesr/2012/silesr2012-002.pdf)\.
references.progress: Appendix A, printed pages 57--100: every nonempty lexical response from the thirteen newly elicited Nimadi lists.
